statement: Let a valid string be a nonempty byte string x such that for some j with 0 <= j < len(words), len(x) <= len(words[j]) and x[t] = words[j][t] for every 0 <= t < len(x). Whenever min_valid_strings returns a result r, r is the minimum number m >= 1 for which there exist valid strings x_1, ..., x_m with target = x_1 ++ ... ++ x_m, where ++ is byte-string concatenation; if no such finite sequence exists, r = -1. Equivalently, r = -1 if and only if target is not a concatenation of one or more valid strings, and if r != -1 then target has a decomposition into exactly r valid strings and none into fewer than r valid strings.
preconditions: All inputs satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(words) <= 100; every words[j] has length between 1 and 50000; sum of lengths of all words is at most 100000; each byte of each word is lowercase ASCII; 1 <= len(target) <= 50000; each byte of target is lowercase ASCII.

Suppose target = x ++ y, where x is a nonempty prefix of some word in words, and there exist k >= 0 and nonempty prefixes y_1, ..., y_k of words in words such that y = y_1 ++ ... ++ y_k (the case k = 0 means y is empty).

statement: Let n = len(target), and for any byte string z let M(z) be the least m >= 0 such that z = z_1 ++ ... ++ z_m for some nonempty prefixes z_1, ..., z_m of words in words, or M(z) = -1 if no such m exists; thus M(empty) = 0. Suppose 0 < p < n and no nonempty prefix of any word in words is equal to the substring target[a..b) for any a, b with 0 <= a < p < b <= n. Then whenever the function returns r, if M(target[0..p)) != -1 and M(target[p..n)) != -1 then r = M(target[0..p)) + M(target[p..n)); otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: All inputs satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(words) <= 100; every words[j] has length between 1 and 50000; sum of lengths of all words is at most 100000; each byte of each word is lowercase ASCII; 1 <= len(target) <= 50000; each byte of target is lowercase ASCII.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (words, target) and returns r' on (words', target), one has r = r'.
preconditions: Inputs (words, target) and (words', target) both satisfy the problem constraints, and words' contains the same multiset of byte strings as words, in any order.

statement: Whenever the function returns r = -1, for every k with 0 < k <= len(target) such that target[0..k) is a nonempty prefix of some word in words, the suffix target[k..len(target)) is not a concatenation of zero or more nonempty prefixes of words in words.
